provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.diagnosis:
The host run failed at the sampling stage, before any factory comparison. The error is 'ValueError: Invalid ARC grid', and there were about 50 rejected seeds. The cause is the constructor's size arithmetic. Panel widths and heights are each drawn from randint(3, 15), with 2 or 3 panels per axis. So width = sum(lengths) + wide - 1 can reach 3*15 + 2 = 47, and height can reach the same. ARC grids are limited to 30. With 3 panels on an axis, the sum averages 27 plus 2 divider lines, so roughly half of those draws are oversized. That explains the high rejection rate.

There is a second, much rarer defect. The holes are i.i.d. with probability 1/10. A full grid row or column inside a panel band can come out entirely 0. It then looks exactly like a divider and splits a panel. The visible input would then define a larger panel grid than the label. A panel could also, in principle, become entirely empty.

The failed factory itself is not implicated in this counterexample. Its divider/run/majority logic is D4-invariant: rows and columns are treated symmetrically, and the output panel grid undergoes the same D4 as the input. It is also palette-correct, since the background is palette[0].
draft_notes.constructor_issue: 1) Bug: generate() emits inputs up to 47x47, which exceeds the 30x30 ARC limit. This is the reported 'Invalid ARC grid' sampling failure. 2) Latent ambiguity: the random 10% holes can very rarely make a non-divider row or column all-zero, or empty a panel. The visible mechanism (full background lines are dividers) would then contradict the patch-grid label. Neither issue affects the canonical fixtures. All four fixtures are at most 28x23, and their zero lines coincide exactly with the intended dividers. The fixtures and labels are consistent with the uniform rule, and no fixture edits are needed. The repair below only changes random sampling. It uses bounded rejection: oversized scenes are rejected, and scenes whose all-zero rows/columns are not exactly the divider lines (or that contain an empty panel) are rejected. Patch colours outside 1..9 are also rejected, as a guard in case common.random_color can return 0. The explicit-argument path and validate() fixtures are unchanged.
draft_notes.explanation: The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates. Full rows and full columns of the background colour (palette[0]) are divider lines. Consecutive dividers merge, and the maximal runs of non-divider lines on each axis form the panel bands. Each row-band x column-band intersection becomes one output cell, coloured with the panel's most frequent non-background colour. The mechanism treats rows and columns symmetrically, and every D4 transform maps the panel lattice to the correspondingly transformed output lattice. So no orientation-specific constants are needed; only the background colour is specialised through the palette. The factory logic is kept from the failed candidate because the host failure came from the constructor, not the solver. The constructor repair rejects scenes larger than 30x30, which caused the sampling error. It also rejects scenes where the hole pattern makes the visible dividers differ from the true panel boundaries, which would make the label disagree with the visible rule.
draft_notes.limitations: None of this has been run; host execution is required. Rejecting oversized scenes conditions the fresh distribution on width <= 30 and height <= 30. With 3 panels on an axis, this biases panel sizes on that axis toward smaller values: the sum of three randint(3, 15) draws must be at most 28. Scenes where hole noise creates a non-divider zero line or an empty panel are also dropped, but these are extremely rare. Sampling is bounded at 1000 attempts and raises RuntimeError on exhaustion, which is practically unreachable because the per-attempt acceptance rate is well above 0.3. The solver's smallest-colour tie-break is never exercised in this domain, because each panel holds only one non-background colour. The rule text mentions stray off-colour cells; the majority vote would handle them, but the constructor never produces them.
draft_notes.host_review: Reviewed size cap and visible-line uniqueness. Host retains sampled panel counts across size retries for 780d0b14; removed deterministic height shrink for 855e0971, which now raises on bounded exhaustion. Original explicit fixtures retained.
